source: Written for this project, NOT AI Video Bootcamp material. Measured from a viral AI cat clip the user supplied (Downloads/snaptik_7679083840794545430_v3.mp4, 10.1 s, 24 fps): no cuts; the wall changes by 0.06 luma per frame and the floor by 0.10 - the camera never moves, not even a handheld drift - while the animals move at a steady ~3.0; motion per second ramps 1.9 -> 2.4 -> 3.0 and holds; the bodies stay planted and the motion lives in the faces, a paw, a swinging tail and a bending feather.
note: Kept out of motion_bank.json, which test_story.py hash-pins. `movements` are merged into the motion bank by build_motion.load_bank() - the locked-off camera is the Cats 'Working cats' format's own lead and detail (story_bank.json formats.trade.camera), so the Videos tab and the Cats trade takes describe a still camera in the same words. `real_motion` is the motion the reference clip has and generated video usually lacks: planted weight, follow-through, real-time speed with a ramp, and a background that holds. `phone_style` replaces the cinema-camera style presets when the phone look is on.

locked-off.name: Locked-off camera (no movement)
locked-off.does: The camera does not move at all - the viral one-take look. The action happens inside one fixed frame, so nothing in the scene can drift or warp.
locked-off.detail: the camera does not move at all for the whole take, only the subject moves
locked-off.example: locked-off camera holding on a ginger cat tickling a mouse with a feather in a back alley, the camera does not move at all for the whole take, only the subject moves

planted.human: feet planted and weight staying grounded, the movement coming from the shoulders, hands and face
planted.animal: bodies planted with real weight on the ground, the movement contained in the faces, paws and tails
planted.object: resting with real weight, shifting only when something pushes it

follow_through.human: hair and loose clothing lagging a beat behind each movement, then settling
follow_through.animal: fur jiggling with each movement, tails swinging and settling a beat later
follow_through.object: loose parts swaying a beat after each movement, then settling

real_motion.tempo: real-time speed with natural motion blur on fast movements, never slow motion, a loose uneven rhythm that starts small and builds over the first second
real_motion.background_still: the background stays completely still, only the subject moves
real_motion.background_moving: the background keeps its shape and position relative to the camera, walls and objects staying solid

phone_style: filmed on an ordinary phone, flat natural colours, everyday phone video quality

story.note: The one-take story: how the user's own 150k-view prompt is written - a short camera opening, then the beats as plain sentences in order with time words (initially... Suddenly... soon after...), ending on 'Subtle, fluid motion.' - no comma list, no second codes, no negatives. build_motion.assemble_story() writes it.
